Amumu.watch: Amumu Q Bandage Toss stops at the first target, so keep minions or jungle monsters between you and Amumu. Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy stuns nearby enemies, so don’t group with allies before Amumu engages. Amumu W Despair deals continuous damage based on your max health while you’re nearby, so don’t stay close for long.
Amumu.build: Get boots first to gain movement speed. Hecarim P Warpath converts bonus movement speed into attack damage, and movement speed also helps you escape Amumu W Despair’s range. Build magic resist against Amumu’s magic damage, but resistances can’t reduce the true damage from Amumu P Cursed Touch.
Amumu.fight: After Amumu Q Bandage Toss or Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is down, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge. Engage while you have bonus movement speed so you can also make use of the attack damage from Hecarim P Warpath. When fighting up close, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal and gain magic resist, but don’t stay in Amumu W Despair’s range longer than necessary.
Amumu.laning: Use your empowered attack to knock Amumu toward your allies, and take advantage of Hecarim E Devastating Charge’s ability to pass through minions when crossing the wave. Allies who need to watch out for Amumu Q Bandage Toss should stand with minions between them and Amumu.
Amumu.combo: Just before engaging, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge, build up enough distance as you run, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear Amumu.
Amumu.escape: Engage during the window when Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy are down. Amumu has no ability to create distance on his own, so you can close in with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows then.
Amumu.teamfight: While Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is available, don’t group with allies; fight in open terrain. Once it’s down, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to enter the enemy backline from the side or behind and disrupt their formation with fear. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread in the middle of the fight, where your allies are also dealing damage, to heal.
Amumu.phase: In the late game, avoid staying in the front for long; look for an entry from the flank.

Brand.watch: Dodge Brand W Pillar of Flame and Brand Q Sear first to make it easier to prevent Brand P Blaze from stacking and detonating. If you’re ablaze, watch out for the stun from Brand Q Sear; move out of the projectile’s path or hide behind minions. When you see Brand R Pyroclasm, spread out from allies to avoid its bounces.
Brand.build: Get boots first to gain movement speed. Hecarim P Warpath converts bonus movement speed into attack damage, and movement speed helps you get out of Brand’s telegraphed attack zones. If you build resistance, get magic resist against Brand’s magic damage.
Brand.fight: Close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge right after Brand W Pillar of Flame is used. If Brand P Blaze hasn’t been applied, Brand Q Sear can’t stun you, making this a good time to engage. Hecarim’s primarily physical damage is effective against Brand’s low armor.
Brand.laning: Standing next to burning minions can let Brand E Conflagration spread to you, so step to the side of the wave. Use your empowered attack to knock Brand toward your allies.
Brand.combo: When Brand W Pillar of Flame is down, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge out of sight and start running. If you can build distance before engaging, charge in with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows and fear Brand on landing, then knock him back with the remaining empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge and hit him with Hecarim Q Rampage. As soon as you get close, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to deal damage and heal.
Brand.escape: Brand has no mobility ability, so engage with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows as soon as Brand W Pillar of Flame is down. If you’re ablaze, dodge the stun from Brand Q Sear before closing the gap.
Brand.phase: In the late game, engage from the side instead of going in head-on.
Brand.teamfight: Before engaging, spread out from allies to reduce the spread of Brand E Conflagration and the bounces from Brand R Pyroclasm. Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to split the enemy backline from the side or behind and fear Brand. When your allies follow up, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and stay in the middle of the fight to heal.

Briar.build: Build armor first against Briar’s main damage. Armor alone can’t stop the magic damage from Briar E Chilling Scream or Briar R Certain Death. If Briar’s healing is preventing you from finishing her off, fit Executioner’s Calling into your build after completing one core item.
Briar.fight: Instead of meeting Briar’s engage head-on, circle around with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and start the fight while you have bonus movement speed. Before going in, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks, then keep landing it during the fight to maintain them. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal in the middle of the fight with your allies.
Briar.laning: Don’t stay in the middle of the lane for long when the area is without vision. Push the lane first, then establish vision so you can turn Briar’s reckless engage into a chance to counterattack.
Briar.combo: Before engaging, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and build up distance as you run, then charge in with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows and fear Briar on landing. Follow up with an empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge to knock her back, then hit her with Hecarim Q Rampage.
Briar.escape: The window before Briar R Certain Death comes back up is your chance to close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Don’t engage just because Briar Q Head Rush is down; also watch for Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack. If Briar charges Briar E Chilling Scream, look for a moment to interrupt it with the fear from Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Briar.phase: In the late game, avoid engaging head-on and start fights from the side.
Briar.teamfight: Keep your back line safe by positioning the frontline between Briar in her W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack state and your back-line damage dealers. From the flank or behind, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear the enemy damage dealers and disrupt their formation. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread where allies and enemies are clustered to heal.
Briar.watch: Briar Q Head Rush stuns and reduces armor and magic resistance, so manage your distance to avoid it. When Briar E Chilling Scream starts charging, don’t stand with your back to a wall. Look for an angle to interrupt the charge with the fear from Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. If you’re the first target hit by Briar R Certain Death, move toward your allies and fight back together rather than fleeing alone.

Ekko.watch: When you see Ekko W Parallel Convergence’s indicator, leave the marked area to prevent its stun and deny Ekko the shield. Ekko Q Timewinder deals more damage on the return hit, so move out of its return path. If Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, don’t overextend to chase him, even when health is low.
Ekko.build: Build magic resistance rather than armor against Ekko’s main damage. If you can’t finish him with a dive because Ekko R Chronobreak heals him, slot in Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Ekko.fight: Dodge Ekko W Parallel Convergence, then look for an opening right after Ekko E Phase Dive closes the gap. Use Hecarim E Devastating Charge to knock him back or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him, forcing out Ekko R Chronobreak. Start the full fight while Ekko R Chronobreak is down and Hecarim E Devastating Charge’s movement speed is still active.
Ekko.laning: After building up enough distance, use your empowered attack to knock Ekko toward your allies. Engage while avoiding the area marked by Ekko W Parallel Convergence’s indicator.
Ekko.combo: If Ekko R Chronobreak is down, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge in advance and run, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Ekko.escape: Don’t engage just because Ekko E Phase Dive is down. Close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows during the window when Ekko W Parallel Convergence and Ekko R Chronobreak are also down.
Ekko.phase: In the late game, avoid engaging head-on and start fights from the side.
Ekko.teamfight: Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to split the enemy formation, including Ekko, and fear them. If Ekko has just closed the gap with Ekko E Phase Dive, respond with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the clumped allies and enemies to heal.

Evelynn.watch: When you see the mark from Evelynn W Allure, back away before the charm lands and alert your allies. If health has decreased, beware of Evelynn R Last Caress, whose damage rises sharply, and do not stay in areas without vision.
Evelynn.build: Prioritize magic resistance against Evelynn’s main damage. Evelynn W Allure reduces magic resistance, and Evelynn E Whiplash deals damage based on your max health, so prioritize movement speed to escape before the mark matures over stacking health. If you can’t finish her with a dive because Evelynn P Demon Shade heals her, slot in Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Evelynn.fight: Use Hecarim E Devastating Charge to circle around and engage while you have movement speed, which also lets you make use of Hecarim P Warpath’s attack damage bonus. If the mark from Evelynn W Allure is maturing, disengage instead of forcing the fight. Before Evelynn R Last Caress comes back up, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Evelynn.combo: Before engaging, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run, then charge in with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear her. Follow up with the empowered attack from the remaining duration of Hecarim E Devastating Charge to knock her back, then use Hecarim Q Rampage. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread as you close in to benefit from its healing and resistance increase during the fight.
Evelynn.escape: Don’t chase just because Evelynn E Whiplash is down. She can still escape with Evelynn R Last Caress, so look for an engage before that ability comes back up. Before the mark from Evelynn W Allure matures, back away first to avoid the charm, then decide whether to engage.
Evelynn.phase: In the late game, you can be quickly burst down if you engage head-on, so start fights from the side.
Evelynn.teamfight: Evelynn targets backline damage dealers, so watch for her engage within your allies’ vision and use Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to catch her. When starting a fight yourself, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to split the enemy damage dealers. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the clumped allies and enemies to heal.
Evelynn.laning: Ward near the jungle camp where she starts fights, and immediately alert your allies when you see Evelynn W Allure’s mark on an ally.

Elise.build: Prioritize magic resistance against Elise’s main damage, and also build some armor to withstand her basic attacks. If you can’t finish her with a dive because Elise P Spider Queen heals her, slot in Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Elise.fight: Right after Elise uses Elise Q Venomous Bite, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. If Elise E Cocoon and Elise E Rappel are both down, turn on her and fight while your movement speed is active to benefit from Hecarim P Warpath’s attack damage bonus. Once close, keep landing Hecarim Q Rampage, and activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal if an ally is attacking with you.
Elise.laning: Elise looks for an advantage with early ganks, so maintain ample vision and don’t push the lane too far when she’s missing. Position yourself so your empowered attack can knock the target toward your allies.
Elise.combo: Before engaging, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run, then charge in with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear her. After landing, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread, then knock Elise back with the remaining empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge and hit her with Hecarim Q Rampage.
Elise.escape: Right after forcing Elise to use Elise Q Venomous Bite, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Once you confirm that both Elise E Cocoon and Elise E Rappel are down, fully commit. While she is airborne with Elise E Rappel, watch where she will land and position yourself to hit her with Hecarim Q Rampage.
Elise.phase: In the early game, watch out for Elise’s ganks, avoid giving up kills, and buy time. In the late game, it's difficult to withstand a prolonged fight head-on, so engage from the side.
Elise.teamfight: Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to split the enemy formation, including Elise, and fear them to help your allies engage. Choose an angle that keeps you from being caught by Elise E Cocoon first. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the clumped allies and enemies to make use of its healing.
Elise.watch: Watch for Elise Q Neurotoxin while you have high health, and Elise Q Venomous Bite when she switches to R Spider Form after your health falls. When you see her transform, manage your distance with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or R Onslaught of Shadows, and activate W Spirit of Dread.

Fiddlesticks.watch: Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm relocates him after channeling and deals area damage. When you see the cast, interrupt it with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows; if you can’t interrupt it, leave its range. If Fiddlesticks has been missing from vision for a while, beware of a brush ambush, and don’t walk past a stationary scarecrow until you’ve checked it.
Fiddlesticks.build: Build magic resistance rather than armor against Fiddlesticks’ ability damage. If you can’t finish him with a dive because of his healing, complete one core item, then slot in Executioner's Calling.
Fiddlesticks.fight: While Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm is down, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and start a fight. If Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest begins, interrupt the channel with your saved Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Fiddlesticks.escape: Don’t rush into areas without vision where Fiddlesticks Q Terrify can hit you.
Fiddlesticks.phase: In the late game, avoid engaging head-on and start fights from the side.
Fiddlesticks.teamfight: Secure vision in the brushes and approaches around objectives, and spread out so you aren’t hit together by Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest, Fiddlesticks E Reap, and Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm. Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to split the enemy damage dealers, and interrupt Fiddlesticks with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows when he starts channeling.
Fiddlesticks.laning: Use your empowered basic attack from a position where you can knock Fiddlesticks toward your allies. Keep vision in the brush behind the lane, and watch out for Fiddlesticks landing a skill on you from out of vision and causing fear.
Fiddlesticks.combo: Just before engaging, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build up stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run in, then charge in with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows and apply fear on landing. Follow up with the empowered basic attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim Q Rampage. If you need to interrupt Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest’s channel, save Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows until then.

Gragas.watch: When you see Gragas Q Barrel Roll, immediately move outside its radius. If Gragas E Body Slam also hits you near the barrel, you take both abilities together, so don’t stay there. When Gragas has R Explosive Cask ready, don’t stand with your back to an enemy turret or the enemy team.
Gragas.build: Finish a core item with attack damage and ability haste first. Against Gragas’s damage, prioritize magic resistance over armor, and avoid building only health because he deals damage based on maximum health. If Gragas P Happy Hour’s healing keeps him from being finished off, fit Executioner’s Calling into your build after completing one core item. Consider penetration against Gragas’s high armor.
Gragas.fight: Right after baiting out Gragas E Body Slam, close the distance with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Hold your burst while Gragas drinks with W Drunken Rage, and unleash it after the damage reduction effect ends. Use Hecarim W Spirit of Dread where enemies and allies are fighting together to make the most of its healing.
Gragas.laning: After building up enough charge, use your empowered attack to push Gragas toward your allies. Don’t stay near Gragas Q Barrel Roll, and if Gragas E Body Slam hits you, move outside the barrel’s radius.
Gragas.combo: Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge out of vision, create distance and run, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear enemies on landing. E remains active after R ends, so use Hecarim E Devastating Charge’s empowered attack to push Gragas toward your allies, then use Hecarim Q Rampage.
Gragas.escape: Right after baiting out Gragas E Body Slam is your chance to engage with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. If Gragas R Explosive Cask is also down, engage while the risk of being knocked away is lower. Gragas can use E Body Slam again if you chase him too far, so only pursue when you can finish him off for sure.
Gragas.phase: Gragas’s sustained damage falls off in the late game, but Hecarim also has trouble withstanding a direct engage, so start fights from the side.
Gragas.teamfight: Avoid narrow passages and brush you have no vision of, and don’t let your backline stand alone within Gragas E Body Slam’s range. Once Gragas E Body Slam is down, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side to split the enemy damage dealers. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and make the most of its healing where allies and enemies are fighting together.

Graves.watch: Graves Q End of the Line detonates immediately when it hits terrain, so don’t fight with your back to a wall or in a narrow passage. If Graves W Smoke Screen traps you, it blocks your vision and slows you, so leave by the shortest route before reengaging. Graves P New Destiny’s basic attack is blocked by the first unit it hits, so fight with minions or allies between you and Graves.
Graves.build: Graves’s main damage is physical, so build armor first and get Plated Steelcaps early.
Graves.fight: Look for a chance to counterattack while Graves is reloading after firing two shots. Fight in open terrain where you have room to dodge Graves Q End of the Line.
Graves.laning: Use your empowered attack to push Graves toward your allies, but don’t hit him as soon as you activate it; build up enough movement first. Apply pressure in lane from the early game to limit Graves’s chances to build growth stacks with Graves E Quickdraw.
Graves.combo: Just before engaging, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run from out of vision, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him.
Graves.escape: Account for the fact that Graves can escape with Graves R Collateral Damage when only Graves E Quickdraw is down. If both of his mobility spells are down, or Graves R Collateral Damage is unavailable, close the distance with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. If Graves W Smoke Screen hits you, leave its area before engaging again.
Graves.phase: Graves gets stronger as he builds stacks, so you’re at a disadvantage as the game goes on. In the late game, Hecarim should look for a flank instead of engaging head-on.
Graves.teamfight: Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to split the enemy damage dealers, fear them, and create an opening for your allies to engage. Against Graves, keep an ally or minion between you and him to block Graves P New Destiny’s basic attack, and watch out for Graves Q End of the Line near walls. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and fight where allies and enemies are clumped together to make use of its healing.

Ivern.watch: If Ivern Q Rootcaller roots you, Ivern’s allies can dash in, so keep minions or terrain between you and Ivern before he throws it. Ivern E Triggerseed leaves a slow after it explodes, so don’t engage the affected target right away. If Ivern R Daisy! starts attacking you, reposition to avoid being knocked up by three consecutive attacks.
Ivern.build: After completing one core item with attack damage and ability haste, fit Quicksilver Sash into your build so you can break free from Ivern Q Rootcaller’s root. If you build resistance against Ivern’s own damage, magic resistance is more effective than armor. However, the real threat is his allies following up on the root and knock-up, so tenacity is often the priority.
Ivern.fight: After baiting out Ivern Q Rootcaller, close the distance with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. If Ivern E Triggerseed is already on a target, engage after the shield explodes. Engage while you have increased movement speed to make the most of Hecarim P Warpath’s attack damage bonus. Focus the shielded ally first rather than chasing Ivern deep.
Ivern.laning: Watch for ambushes near newly created brush and clear vision there.
Ivern.combo: Before engaging, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run far enough, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear enemies. Use the empowered attack from your remaining Hecarim E Devastating Charge to knock them back, then use Hecarim Q Rampage. In a clumped fight, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread so damage from your allies also contributes to your healing.
Ivern.phase: In the late game, avoid engaging head-on and start fights from the side.
Ivern.teamfight: Dodge or bait out Ivern Q Rootcaller, then use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side to split the enemy damage dealers and fear them. Wait for Ivern E Triggerseed to explode on its target, and reposition if Ivern R Daisy! hits you with consecutive attacks. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread where allies and enemies are fighting together to heal.
Ivern.escape: Ivern Q Rootcaller is his only mobility ability, so the moment after you make him use it is your window to engage. Delay your engage on a target affected by Ivern E Triggerseed until the shield explodes.

Karthus.watch: Walking through Karthus W Wall of Pain slows you and reduces your magic resistance, so go around it. Karthus Q Lay Waste deals more damage when it hits you alone, so dodge its telegraphed area. Right after killing Karthus, move away from his corpse to avoid attacks from Karthus P Death Defied. Keep enough health after a fight to survive Karthus R Requiem.
Karthus.build: Get boots that grant movement speed first and use them to engage and dodge area attacks. Against Karthus’s damage, prioritize magic resistance over armor. It’s also important to avoid Karthus W Wall of Pain and quickly leave the area of Karthus E Defile.
Karthus.fight: Close the distance with Hecarim E Devastating Charge while you have increased movement speed. If you kill Karthus, stay away from his corpse until Karthus P Death Defied ends.
Karthus.laning: When ganking, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge out of vision and circle around toward Karthus’s escape route, then use your empowered attack to push him toward your allies.
Karthus.escape: Karthus has no mobility or immobilizing abilities, so look for chances to close the distance. If Karthus W Wall of Pain is placed, don’t walk through it; engage from around it with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Karthus.phase: In the early game, pressure Karthus with ganks or jungle invades before he scales. In the late game, avoid engaging head-on and start fights from the side.
Karthus.teamfight: Position yourself so you don’t stay in Karthus E Defile for long, and move immediately after killing him to avoid attacks from Karthus P Death Defied. Engage from the side or behind with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear and disrupt the enemy formation. In the middle of a fight where allies and enemies are clumped together, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal.
Karthus.combo: From out of sight, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and cover some distance while running. Engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear enemies on landing, then use the remaining empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge to push Karthus and follow up with Hecarim Q Rampage.

Jax.watch: When Jax E Counter Strike is active, it negates basic attacks and Hecarim E Devastating Charge’s empowered attack. You can also be hit by an AoE stun when it is recast. Move out of stun range and wait for the duration to end.
Jax.build: Jax’s damage relies on basic attacks and attack speed, so consider reducing his attack speed first. Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so build both armor and magic resistance. Jax E Counter Strike deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid stacking health alone.
Jax.fight: Start trading after Jax E Counter Strike is down. While it is active, focus on ability damage, such as Hecarim Q Rampage. Engage while you have bonus movement speed to use Hecarim P Warpath’s attack damage bonus, and keep landing Hecarim Q Rampage to maintain its stacks.
Jax.laning: Jax has the advantage in a level 1 melee trade, so don’t force an engage. Pressure him with your ally once Jax E Counter Strike is down.
Jax.combo: After Jax E Counter Strike ends, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him. Use the empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge that remains after R ends to knock Jax back, then use Hecarim Q Rampage. If you hit a jungle monster with Q just before the fight to build stacks, you can use Q more frequently after engaging.
Jax.escape: Right after Jax uses Jax Q Leap Strike is an opportunity to close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. If Jax E Counter Strike is active, delay your engage and save a movement ability to get out of stun range. Go in again after Counter Strike ends.
Jax.phase: In the late game, Hecarim should avoid engaging from the front and start fights from the flank.
Jax.teamfight: If Jax activates Jax E Counter Strike and dives in, don’t group up and get hit by the AoE stun together. Focus crowd control on him after Counter Strike ends. Hecarim should split the enemy backline from the flank with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the clashing teams to heal.

JarvanIV.watch: Jarvan’s flag can fly over walls, so if he disappears from vision, watch positions near walls too.
JarvanIV.fight: Engage with the movement speed from Hecarim E Devastating Charge to make use of Hecarim P Warpath’s attack damage bonus. When fighting with allies, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to gain armor and heal from damage dealt by your allies as well.
JarvanIV.laning: Position yourself so your empowered attack can knock the opponent toward your allies.
JarvanIV.combo: Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and build up distance while running from out of vision. If Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows is available, run with E, then fear them with R and follow up with E’s empowered attack and Q.
JarvanIV.teamfight: Fear the enemy backline with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the flank or behind to disrupt their formation. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the clashing teams to heal.

LeeSin.watch: If health is below half, stay close to your team or an allied turret while Lee Sin's second cast is available. Before a team fight, create space so Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage doesn’t knock you into an ally.
LeeSin.fight: If you meet Lee Sin in the early jungle, don’t take the duel; back off. Start fights with the movement speed from Hecarim E Devastating Charge, then focus your damage right after Lee Sin uses Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will to engage. When fighting in the middle of a melee with allies, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal.
LeeSin.laning: Use your empowered attack to push Lee Sin toward your team, and dodge the straight-line angle of Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike by keeping minions between you.
LeeSin.escape: After Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike misses, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows before it comes back. Lee Sin can also escape with Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will, so don’t assume he has no escape just because Q is down. If Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage is also down, there’s less risk of being kicked away.
LeeSin.phase: Lee Sin is strong in early duels, so back off if you meet him in the jungle and take objectives and lane advantages instead. Lee Sin falls off later, but Hecarim also struggles to engage head-on, so start fights from the flank.
LeeSin.teamfight: From the flank or behind, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to split the enemy damage dealers and fear them to help your team engage. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and fight in the melee to heal. Keep space between you and allies so Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage doesn’t kick one of them into you.
LeeSin.build: Build armor first to mitigate the physical damage from Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike and Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage. Armor cannot block the magic damage from Lee Sin E Tempest / Cripple. If the root from Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage interrupts your movement, fit a Quicksilver Sash in after one core item.
LeeSin.combo: Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge out of vision, run for a while, then approach. If Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows is available, run with E, use R to fear, then follow up with the remaining E empowered attack and Q.

MasterYi.watch: Master Yi can’t be targeted while using Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, so use Hecarim E Devastating Charge's empowered attack right after he lands. When Master Yi R Highlander is active, slows don’t work on him, and Master Yi E Wuju Style's empowered attacks deal some true damage, so avoid staying in an extended fight with him.
MasterYi.build: Master Yi E Wuju Style's true damage can’t be reduced by resistances, so build some health too. If Master Yi W Meditate's healing keeps you from finishing him, fit Executioner's Calling in after completing one core item.
MasterYi.fight: After making Master Yi use Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows as he lands. Engage while you have bonus movement speed so you can also use the attack damage from Hecarim P Warpath. If Master Yi activates Master Yi W Meditate, interrupt it with Hecarim E Devastating Charge's knockback or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows' fear.
MasterYi.laning: If Master Yi has already used Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, push him toward your team with an empowered attack after he lands. Hitting him immediately from the front shortens the distance traveled with Hecarim E Devastating Charge, weakening its damage and knockback distance.
MasterYi.combo: Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge early and run in. Engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows as Master Yi Q Alpha Strike ends and he lands. If you built stacks by hitting a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage just before engaging, use Q again at short intervals during the fight.
MasterYi.phase: Master Yi is weak in early jungle fights and ganks, so fight him if you meet him or take early objectives to slow his growth. Master Yi gets strong later, while Hecarim struggles to withstand a head-on engage, so look for a flank.
MasterYi.teamfight: Move with your team to avoid giving Master Yi his first takedown participation. Once Master Yi Q Alpha Strike ends and he lands, stop his engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows' fear or Hecarim E Devastating Charge's knockback, and save crowd control for Master Yi W Meditate. If the fight becomes a melee, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to turn the damage your allies deal into healing too.
MasterYi.escape: Right after you force Master Yi to use Master Yi Q Alpha Strike is your chance to engage. Close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows, but don’t rush your empowered attack during Master Yi Q Alpha Strike; wait for him to land.

MonkeyKing.watch: Wukong E Nimbus Strike is targeted, so you cannot dodge it within range. If the follow-up Wukong Q Crushing Blow reduces your armor, trades become unfavorable. After Wukong W Warrior Trickster, don’t use abilities on the clone left in place; watch which way the real Wukong escapes.
MonkeyKing.build: Build armor first against Wukong’s main damage, while keeping in mind that armor won’t block the magic damage from Wukong E Nimbus Strike. If Wukong’s healing prevents you from finishing a dive, complete one core item, then fit in Executioner’s Calling.
MonkeyKing.fight: Wukong gains armor and healing as he hits champions, so repeatedly engage briefly and disengage for short trades instead of taking extended duels. Engage and deal damage while Hecarim E Devastating Charge’s movement speed is active. If Wukong W Warrior Trickster makes the real Wukong disappear, don’t waste abilities on the clone.
MonkeyKing.laning: Use an empowered basic attack to knock Wukong toward your team, but account for his ability to escape if both Wukong W Warrior Trickster and Wukong E Nimbus Strike are available.
MonkeyKing.combo: While Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge, build up distance, then charge in with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Don’t attack as soon as you activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge; build up some distance first.
MonkeyKing.escape: The window while Wukong W Warrior Trickster is on cooldown is your chance to close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Check whether Wukong E Nimbus Strike is also down before going in. Force an objective or fight immediately after Wukong R Cyclone has been fully spent.
MonkeyKing.phase: In the late game, start fights from the flank instead of engaging head-on, and don’t group with your team while Wukong R Cyclone is available.
MonkeyKing.teamfight: If Wukong R Cyclone is ready, spread out from your team so he can’t knock up several of you at once. Split the enemy’s back line with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the flank or behind, then activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread after engaging to heal amid the clash of allies and enemies. Look for a chance to force a fight immediately after Wukong R Cyclone has been fully spent.

Nidalee.watch: Nidalee Q Javelin Toss deals more damage the farther it travels, so sidestep its path or keep your team’s frontline between you and Nidalee. Stepping on Nidalee W Bushwhack or getting hit by her spear marks you as hunted. If marked, save Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows for when Nidalee uses W Pounce to jump in.
Nidalee.build: Magic resistance is more effective than armor against Nidalee’s main damage, so build magic resistance. If healing from Nidalee E Primal Surge prevents you from finishing her, complete one core item, then fit in Executioner’s Calling.
Nidalee.fight: Avoid Nidalee Q Javelin Toss and Nidalee W Bushwhack so you can start the fight without a hunt mark.
Nidalee.laning: Use an empowered basic attack to knock Nidalee toward your team, but clear traps along jungle entrances and in the river in advance with a Control Ward or an area-of-effect ability.
Nidalee.combo: Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run far enough, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear her on landing. Follow with an empowered basic attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge to knock her back, then hit her with Hecarim Q Rampage.
Nidalee.escape: Immediately after making Nidalee use W Pounce, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Nidalee has no crowd control, so dodge her spear and traps, then use the window after her mobility is spent to engage.
Nidalee.phase: Come online in the mid game, when you gain attack damage and ability haste. In the late game, avoid engaging head-on and start fights from the flank.
Nidalee.teamfight: Remember where Nidalee stepped out to throw her spear, then engage from the flank with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear her. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and fight amid the clash of allies and enemies to heal.

Nunu.watch: Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! rolls in from far away and knocks you up. When you see it, move toward the snowball and escape through the path Nunu & Willump came from instead of running straight back. If Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage hits you, its root detonates later, so immediately use Hecarim E Devastating Charge to get out of the area. When Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero starts, interrupt the channel with the fear from Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows or leave its area.
Nunu.build: Build magic resistance first against Nunu & Willump’s main damage. If the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage stops your engages, fit Quicksilver Sash in after one core item. If healing from Nunu & Willump Q Consume prevents you from finishing them, complete one core item, then buy Executioner’s Calling.
Nunu.fight: Hecarim deals more damage while he has movement speed, so activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and charge in. Keep moving and fighting before you’re rooted by Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, and activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread when you’re on top of them with your team to heal based on the damage they take. Nunu & Willump has no ability to create distance, so when you have an opening, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Nunu.laning: Keep in mind that Nunu & Willump can return for another gank immediately after an initial gank.
Nunu.combo: Just before engaging, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge out of vision and build up speed, then charge in with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear them on landing. Knock them back with the empowered basic attack from the remaining duration of Hecarim E Devastating Charge, then hit them with Hecarim Q Rampage. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread as you reach them to heal during the fight.
Nunu.escape: Dodge the knockup from Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and wait until Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage’s root is also down. That’s your opening: Nunu & Willump has no ability to create distance, so close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Nunu.phase: In the late game, it’s hard to survive a head-on engage, so start fights from the flank.
Nunu.teamfight: Engage from the flank or behind with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear the enemy back line and disrupt their formation. If Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero starts channeling, you can interrupt it with the fear from Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. If you can’t interrupt it, leave its area. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the clash of allies and enemies to heal.

Poppy.build: Build armor first against Poppy’s main damage. Poppy Q Hammer Shock deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that only stack a lot of health. Don’t invest separately in magic resistance just for Poppy.
Poppy.fight: Close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge after Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends and Poppy E Heroic Charge is used. Engage while your movement speed is active to make use of the attack damage from Hecarim P Warpath. In close combat, keep hitting Poppy with Hecarim Q Rampage, and walk out of the area of Poppy Q Hammer Shock.
Poppy.laning: Position yourself in an open area so Poppy E Heroic Charge can’t knock you into a wall and stun you. When the shield from Poppy P Iron Ambassador drops, step on it first to prevent Poppy from gaining the shield.
Poppy.combo: Once Poppy W Steadfast Presence has ended, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge, build up speed, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread as you reach the enemy to help you heal during the fight.
Poppy.escape: Right after you force Poppy to use Poppy E Heroic Charge is your chance to close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. However, if Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, wait for it to end before charging, and if Poppy R Keeper's Verdict is charging, first move out of its line of fire.
Poppy.phase: Hecarim hits his peak in the mid game, when he has attack damage and ability haste, so take advantage of windows when Poppy W Steadfast Presence and Poppy E Heroic Charge are down. In the late game, it’s difficult to hold out on the frontline for long, so look for flanks.
Poppy.teamfight: Don’t charge into an area where Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active. After it ends, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to split the line of enemy damage dealers. Once the fear disrupts their formation, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and fight where allies and enemies are clustered to make use of the healing. If Poppy R Keeper's Verdict is charging, move sideways out of its line of fire.
Poppy.watch: If you charge with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows while Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, it will be blocked and you won’t be able to use movement abilities for a short time, so wait for it to end or walk up. Poppy E Heroic Charge stuns you if it knocks you into a wall, so don’t put a wall behind you. If you’re hit by the first part of Poppy Q Hammer Shock, walk out of the zone before the second damage triggers. If Poppy R Keeper's Verdict is charging, move sideways out of its line of fire.

Rammus.watch: When you see Rammus Q Powerball, keep minions between you and him to block his approach. Rammus E Frenzying Taunt prevents movement and ability use after it hits, so stay out of range. Give Rammus R Soaring Slam, cast after he closes in quickly with Rammus Q Powerball, plenty of room, and move away from the landing spot immediately.
Rammus.build: Build magic resistance first to prepare for the magic damage from Rammus Q Powerball, Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl, and Rammus R Soaring Slam. If you’re repeatedly caught by crowd control such as Rammus E Frenzying Taunt, consider tenacity too. If you need to penetrate Rammus’s resistances, choose percentage penetration over flat penetration.
Rammus.fight: When Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active, don’t use empowered basic attacks; wait for its duration to end. Build speed and an entry angle with Hecarim E Devastating Charge from outside Rammus E Frenzying Taunt range, then focus your damage after Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl ends. Keep landing Hecarim Q Rampage during the fight to maintain its stacks.
Rammus.combo: Out of vision, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run to create distance, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear the enemy. If Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active, don’t rush an empowered basic attack; attack after it ends.
Rammus.escape: While Rammus R Soaring Slam is on cooldown, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. It’s a good time to engage and deal damage if Rammus E Frenzying Taunt is on cooldown and Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl has ended.
Rammus.phase: In the late game, avoid engaging from the front and start fights from the side.
Rammus.teamfight: Don’t pour attacks into Rammus while Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active. Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to split the enemy damage dealers. Once the fear disrupts their formation, your allies can engage, and Hecarim can activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the fight to heal. Don’t stay where Rammus R Soaring Slam lands.

RekSai.watch: When Rek'Sai goes underground with Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, watch for the moment she emerges and knocks you up. Avoid walls and narrow paths. When she surfaces, use Hecarim E Devastating Charge or R Onslaught of Shadows to move and dodge the knock-up. Stay close to allies after Rek'Sai damages you, since Rek'Sai R Void Rush may follow immediately.
RekSai.build: Build armor first to account for the physical damage from Rek'Sai Q Queen's Wrath / Prey Seeker and R Void Rush. Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel deals true damage, which resistances can’t reduce, and R Void Rush scales with your maximum health, so avoid choices that only add a large amount of health. If Rek'Sai’s healing is stopping you from finishing her off, fit Executioner's Calling in after completing one core item.
RekSai.fight: After dodging the knock-up from Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, keep dealing damage to limit her opportunities to heal while Burrowed.
RekSai.laning: Early on, keep Rek'Sai’s ganks in mind: don’t move alone without vision or push your lane too aggressively. Walk over visible tunnel entrances as you pass to remove Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel’s entry and escape routes.
RekSai.combo: Just before engaging, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge in advance and run in, then use R Onslaught of Shadows to engage and fear the enemy. Push them toward your allies with the remaining empowered basic attack from E, then use Q.
RekSai.escape: Dodge the knock-up from Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, then engage after Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel and R Void Rush are on cooldown. If only one mobility ability is down, she can escape with the other, so wait longer. In particular, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and R Onslaught of Shadows before Rek'Sai R Void Rush comes back up.
RekSai.phase: Early on, watch for Rek'Sai’s ganks, avoid giving up kills, and stall for time. In the late game, it’s hard to hold out in a prolonged fight from the front, so look for a flank.
RekSai.teamfight: Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to fear the enemy damage dealers and disrupt their formation. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the fight to heal from damage dealt by your allies as well. While Rek'Sai is leaping with Rek'Sai R Void Rush, don’t rush your attacks; follow up as she lands with area damage such as Hecarim Q Rampage.

Rengar.watch: Rengar P Unseen Predator lets him leap from brush and build Ferocity, so avoid paths beside brush when Rengar is out of sight. At full Ferocity, Rengar E Bola Strike roots, and Rengar W Battle Roar can remove crowd control, so don’t start a fight while he’s in that state. Watch out for Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt, and don’t move alone at low health.
Rengar.build: Build armor first to prepare for Rengar’s main damage. If Rengar E Bola Strike’s root is stopping you from engaging, fit Quicksilver Sash in after one core item. If Rengar W Battle Roar’s healing is stopping you from finishing him off, consider Executioner's Calling at the same point.
Rengar.fight: Trade when Rengar has no Ferocity or after Rengar W Battle Roar is on cooldown. Dodge Rengar E Bola Strike, then build speed and engage with Hecarim E Devastating Charge. If Rengar W Battle Roar is down, keep him in range with the fear from Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows and the knockback from Hecarim E Devastating Charge, and fight with Hecarim W Spirit of Dread active.
Rengar.laning: When Rengar is out of sight, avoid paths beside brush and use a Control Ward to reveal the brush. Once you’re on him, push Rengar toward your allies with an empowered basic attack.
Rengar.combo: Dodge Rengar E Bola Strike and confirm that Rengar W Battle Roar is on cooldown, then activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run in. Charge with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear enemies on landing, then knock Rengar back with the remaining empowered basic attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge and hit him with Hecarim Q Rampage. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread as you reach him to heal during the fight.
Rengar.escape: After dodging Rengar E Bola Strike, you have a window to engage with Hecarim E Devastating Charge. If Rengar W Battle Roar is also on cooldown and he has no Ferocity, keep him in range with the fear from Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows and the knockback from Hecarim E Devastating Charge. Use this opening, since Rengar has no ability to create distance on his own.
Rengar.phase: In the late game, look for a flank instead of engaging from the front. The available information isn’t enough to determine which of the two champions is stronger at each stage of the game.
Rengar.teamfight: Move with allies and stay within vision to spot Rengar engaging with Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt. Keep your backline behind your frontline. After stopping Rengar’s engage, wait for Rengar W Battle Roar to go on cooldown, then flank with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him and knock him back with Hecarim E Devastating Charge. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the fight to heal.

Sejuani.watch: Sejuani Q Arctic Assault can knock you airborne, and Sejuani R Glacial Prison can stun you, interrupting your engage. When you see their wind-up, move sideways to dodge. If Sejuani W Winter's Wrath hits you with its first strike, get out of range before the second strike, which carries a slow and heavy damage. Sejuani E Permafrost stacks can also build from basic attacks by allied melee champions, so create distance when the indicator fills.
Sejuani.build: Build magic resistance first to prepare for damage from Sejuani P Fury of the North, Q Arctic Assault, and E Permafrost. Sejuani W Winter's Wrath deals physical damage, so magic resistance won’t block it. In the mid game, secure attack damage and ability haste, Hecarim’s strengths.
Sejuani.fight: If Sejuani’s Frost Armor is active, deal damage first with Hecarim Q Rampage, then engage with Hecarim E Devastating Charge after the armor is removed. Close the gap after Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is on cooldown, and keep landing Hecarim Q Rampage during the fight to maintain its stacks. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread where your allies are also dealing damage to heal.
Sejuani.laning: Use an empowered basic attack after building up movement distance to knock Sejuani toward your allies, but watch for Sejuani Q Arctic Assault if it’s still available.
Sejuani.combo: Just before engaging, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run in, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear the enemy. Push them toward your allies with the remaining empowered basic attack from E, then hit them with Q. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread as you reach them to heal from your allies’ damage too.
Sejuani.escape: The moment Sejuani Q Arctic Assault goes on cooldown is an opportunity to close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or R Onslaught of Shadows. If Sejuani E Permafrost’s stacks are building or Sejuani R Glacial Prison is still available, account for the risk of being caught by crowd control before engaging.
Sejuani.phase: Early on, Sejuani’s kill and damage metrics are low, so focus on jungle control and objectives to delay her item timings. In the late game, avoid engaging from the front and start fights from the side.
Sejuani.teamfight: Instead of trying to break through Sejuani from the front, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to fear the enemy damage dealers. Watch Sejuani Q Arctic Assault and R Glacial Prison as you engage, then activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the fight to heal after you go in.

Shaco.watch: Watch for the fear from Shaco W Jack In The Box in bushes without vision and around objectives. Clear the boxes with a Control Ward or Oracle Lens before entering. If the clone from Shaco R Hallucinate dies, take a step back to avoid the explosion and boxes.
Shaco.build: Build magic resistance first to prepare for the damage from Shaco W Jack In The Box, E Two-Shiv Poison, and R Hallucinate. Get movement-speed boots and also build health so you can escape dangerous positions and prepare for Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison, which gets stronger when health is low.
Shaco.fight: Focus Shaco with your allies as soon as he reveals himself after Shaco Q Deceive. Approach with the movement speed from Hecarim E Devastating Charge, and keep landing Hecarim Q Rampage during the fight to maintain its stacks.
Shaco.laning: Keep vision at your jungle entrances to prepare for Shaco's early invades and ganks.
Shaco.combo: Once Shaco Q Deceive is down, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run to create distance, then enter with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Fear him on landing, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread, knock him back with the empowered basic attack you still have from E, then use Hecarim Q Rampage.
Shaco.escape: The moment after you make Shaco use Shaco Q Deceive is your window to engage. Clear Shaco W Jack In The Box from entry routes without vision first, then close in on Shaco while Q is down with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or R Onslaught of Shadows.
Shaco.phase: Early on, watch for Shaco's ganks and invades, avoid giving up kills, and secure objectives. In the late game, start fights from the flank instead of going in head-on.
Shaco.teamfight: Focus Shaco with your allies the moment he enters with Shaco Q Deceive. Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to enter from the side or behind and disrupt the enemy formation with fear, then activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal in the middle of the ensuing team fight.

Skarner.fight: Right after you make Skarner use Skarner E Ixtal's Impact, close the distance with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Enter with your movement speed active to also gain attack damage from Hecarim P Warpath.
Skarner.laning: Use your empowered basic attack to knock Skarner toward your allies, but avoid positions where Skarner E Ixtal's Impact could catch you and slam you into a wall. A short, head-on charge weakens the damage and knockback from Hecarim E Devastating Charge.
Skarner.combo: Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run, then charge in with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear them. After landing, knock them toward your allies with the remaining empowered basic attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge and use Hecarim Q Rampage. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal while fighting in the middle of the scrum with your allies.
Skarner.escape: The moment after Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down is your chance to go in with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. If Skarner R Impale is still available, you can't escape its suppression with a movement ability, so check your entry position and your distance from Skarner's allies first.
Skarner.phase: Early on, contest jungle control and objectives to delay Skarner's item timings. In the late game, look for a flank because it's difficult to hold out for long when engaging head-on.
Skarner.teamfight: Don't try to break through Skarner head-on. Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to split the enemy damage dealers and fear them. Enter from a position where Skarner E Ixtal's Impact can't push you into a wall and Skarner R Impale can't pull you away. After you engage, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal in the middle of the fight while your allies deal damage alongside you.
Skarner.build: First decide whether you need a way to remove Skarner R Impale’s suppression. If you do, consider Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar as listed in the data. For resistance, build magic resistance first against the damage from Skarner P Threads of Vibration, Skarner W Seismic Bastion, and Skarner R Impale. Skarner P Threads of Vibration and Skarner Q Shattered Earth / Upheaval deal damage based on your maximum health, so be cautious about choices that only increase health.

Shyvana.watch: Watch out for the slow and maximum-health-based damage from Shyvana E Molten Burst, and keep your distance so you don't repeatedly take empowered attacks from Shyvana Q Emberstrike. Shyvana is unstoppable while flying in with Shyvana R Dragon's Descent, so don't try to interrupt her engage; catch her after she lands with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Shyvana.build: Build magic resistance first to prepare for the magic damage from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis, E Molten Burst, and R Dragon's Descent. Get armor to prepare for her basic attack damage, but don't rely on stacking health alone because she has maximum-health-based damage. If Shyvana's healing prevents you from finishing her off, fit Executioner's Calling into your build after completing one core item.
Shyvana.fight: Pressure Shyvana when her Fury bar is empty, and don't start an objective in front of her when it's full. Counterattack once Shyvana R Dragon's Descent ends and she returns to human form.
Shyvana.laning: Pressure Shyvana early to take jungle camps and objectives before she can build stacks of Shyvana P Scalemail.
Shyvana.combo: Just before engaging, land Hecarim Q Rampage on a jungle monster to build stacks.
Shyvana.escape: You can't stop Shyvana with Hecarim's crowd control while she's flying in with Shyvana R Dragon's Descent, so target her after she lands. When Shyvana's Fury bar is empty and she can't transform, close the distance and catch her with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Shyvana.phase: Early on, Shyvana is weakest before she has stacks, so pressure her camps and objectives. In the late game, her permanent stacks from Shyvana P Scalemail put you at a greater disadvantage, so look for a flank instead of engaging head-on.
Shyvana.teamfight: In Shyvana's dragon form, spread out with your allies so several of you don't get hit together by the path of Shyvana R Dragon's Descent, the explosion from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis, or Shyvana E Molten Burst. Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to split the enemy damage dealers, then activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and fight where your allies and enemies are clustered together after you land.

Taliyah.build: Build magic resistance first because the main damage from Taliyah Q Threaded Volley and E Unraveled Earth is magic. Hecarim W Spirit of Dread also increases your magic resistance and heals you during a fight, so activate it when fighting up close.
Taliyah.fight: First find an entry angle that avoids the rocky ground from Taliyah E Unraveled Earth. Approaching with the movement speed from Hecarim E Devastating Charge also increases your attack damage through Hecarim P Warpath, making it a good way to deal physical damage to Taliyah, who has low armor. Move sideways out of the direction Taliyah Q Threaded Volley is coming from.
Taliyah.laning: Position yourself so your empowered basic attack can knock Taliyah toward your allies, but go around your charge path if Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is set up there. If Taliyah disappears from the jungle, suspect that she may use Taliyah P Rock Surfing and Taliyah R Weaver's Wall to influence another lane, and back off in advance.
Taliyah.combo: Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge early and run from out of vision, then use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows along a path that avoids the rocky ground to fear her on landing. Hecarim E Devastating Charge's remaining duration pauses during Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows, so after landing, knock Taliyah toward your allies with the empowered basic attack and use Hecarim Q Rampage. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread as you get on top of her to use its healing and increased resistances.
Taliyah.escape: Don't immediately go in just because only one of Taliyah E Unraveled Earth and Taliyah R Weaver's Wall has been used. In particular, close the distance with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows before Taliyah R Weaver's Wall returns, when you can avoid the rocky ground from Taliyah E Unraveled Earth. If you've already damaged Taliyah, keep up the damage to deny her a chance to escape with Taliyah R Weaver's Wall.
Taliyah.phase: Hecarim peaks in the mid game, when he gains attack damage and ability haste, so actively look for angles to get on top of Taliyah. In the late game, avoid engaging head-on and start fights from the flank.
Taliyah.teamfight: Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the side or behind to fear Taliyah's line of damage dealers and disrupt their formation. Choose an entry angle that avoids charging through Taliyah E Unraveled Earth. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and fight where your allies and enemies are clustered together to make use of its healing.
Taliyah.watch: Go around the rocky ground instead of using Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows across it. Taliyah Q Threaded Volley cannot change direction while casting, so don’t approach in a straight line; dodge to the side.

Udyr.watch: Watch for Udyr E Blazing Stampede's stun right after he activates it. Udyr Q Wilding Claw and Udyr R Wingborne Storm deal damage based on your max health, so don't fight him for long. Udyr W Iron Mantle's shield and healing can also delay the finish.
Udyr.build: Build armor first to account for Udyr's main damage. However, Udyr R Wingborne Storm deals magic damage, and Udyr Q Wilding Claw deals both damage types, so armor alone won't block everything. If his healing keeps you from finishing him after a dive, fit Executioner's Calling into your build after completing one core item.
Udyr.fight: Once the shield from Udyr W Iron Mantle is gone, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and press the attack. Stack Hecarim Q Rampage before the fight and keep landing it throughout.
Udyr.laning: When Udyr is missing, track his path with vision at key routes and jungle entrances, and don't overextend in lane. Use your empowered attack to push him toward your team.
Udyr.combo: Just before the fight, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run in, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him. After landing, use the empowered attack from the remaining Hecarim E Devastating Charge to push him back, then hit him with Hecarim Q Rampage.
Udyr.phase: In the late game, avoid engaging from the front and start fights from the flank.
Udyr.teamfight: Don't try to burst down Udyr first when he has defensive items and Udyr W Iron Mantle's shield. Use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the flank or behind to split the enemy damage dealers and let your team engage while they're scattered by the fear. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and heal in the middle of the tangled fight.
Udyr.escape: Right after you force Udyr to use Udyr E Blazing Stampede is your window to close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. If you’ve already been stunned once by Udyr E Blazing Stampede, counterattack or escape while it cannot stun the same target again. Immobilizing effects do not work during Udyr’s E Awakening, so use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him after it ends.

Vi.watch: When Vi charges Vi Q Vault Breaker, back away or sidestep to dodge it. Vi W Denting Blows reduces a target's armor and increases her attack speed as she keeps hitting them, so don't fight her for long. Save Hecarim E Devastating Charge's knockback while Vi is charging in with Vi R Cease and Desist, and use it after the knock-up ends.
Vi.build: Build armor first because Vi Q Vault Breaker, Vi W Denting Blows, and Vi E Relentless Force deal primarily physical damage. Vi W Denting Blows deals damage based on your max health and reduces your armor, so avoid stacking health alone. Her basic attacks and attack speed drive her damage, so consider effects that reduce attack speed as well.
Vi.fight: Immediately after dodging or baiting out Vi Q Vault Breaker, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge. Don't trade for long enough to stack Vi W Denting Blows; attack briefly, then create distance. When fighting with your team, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the enemies to benefit from its healing and armor increase.
Vi.laning: Position yourself to push Vi toward your team with an empowered attack. If Vi enters after hitting a minion with an ability to activate Vi P Blast Shield, trade after the shield is gone.
Vi.combo: Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge in advance and run, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows during the opening when Vi Q Vault Breaker is unavailable. If you hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage just before going in to build stacks, you can use them in the follow-up attack.
Vi.phase: In the late game, avoid engaging from the front and start fights from the flank.
Vi.teamfight: Vi R Cease and Desist pursues its chosen target until it reaches them, so don't let your backline damage dealers wander out of vision alone. From the flank or behind, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear the enemy damage dealers and scatter their formation. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread in the middle of the fight where your team can reach enemies, and heal.
Vi.escape: Right after you force Vi to use Q Vault Breaker or dodge it is your chance to engage with Hecarim E Devastating Charge. If Vi R Cease and Desist has started, don’t try to knock her back as she charges in; use Hecarim E Devastating Charge after she lands and the knock-up ends.

Viego.watch: Viego W Spectral Maw stuns for longer the longer he charges it, so sidestep when you see him charging. He moves more slowly while charging, and the charge is interrupted if he's disrupted, so if you can reach him, interrupt it with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. When your health is low, back away because you may be targeted by Viego R Heartbreaker.
Viego.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Viego Q Blade of the Ruined King and Viego R Heartbreaker. Viego W Spectral Maw deals magic damage, which armor can't block. If healing from Viego P Sovereign's Domination and Viego Q Blade of the Ruined King keeps you from finishing him, fit Executioner's Calling into your build after completing one core item.
Viego.fight: Start the fight with the movement speed from Hecarim E Devastating Charge to make the most of Hecarim P Warpath's bonus attack damage. If Viego charges Viego W Spectral Maw, sidestep or interrupt it with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Viego.laning: After building up enough running distance, use your empowered attack to push Viego toward your team. If you see the black mist from Viego E Harrowed Path along the terrain, avoid that route or place a Control Ward there, and don't push the lane in that direction.
Viego.combo: Just before going in, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to fill your stacks. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run in, then charge in with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him. Push Viego back with the empowered attack from the remaining Hecarim E Devastating Charge, then hit him with Hecarim Q Rampage. Once you're on him, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal during the fight.
Viego.escape: Don't engage just because Viego W Spectral Maw is down. Close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows when Viego R Heartbreaker is also down or before it comes back up. If you can't win the skirmish, retreat and deny Viego the chance to get a takedown and possess someone.
Viego.phase: In the late game, it's hard to engage from the front and survive, so take the flank and avoid fights that would give Viego a takedown.
Viego.teamfight: From the flank or behind, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to split the enemy damage dealers and open the engage with fear. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and heal where your team and the enemy are tangled together. If an ally falls, push Viego away with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or lock him down with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows so he can't reach the wraith left there, and don't continue fighting near that spot.

Warwick.watch: While Warwick E Primal Howl is active, he takes reduced damage and fears you when it ends, so don't charge in and unload burst with Hecarim E Devastating Charge. If Warwick R Infinite Duress hits you, you can't do anything while suppressed, and he can reach from farther away when his movement speed is higher. When health falls below half, Warwick W Blood Hunt exposes your position, so don't linger while health is substantially depleted.
Warwick.build: Build magic resistance first against the magic damage from Warwick P Eternal Hunger, Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, and Warwick R Infinite Duress. Build some armor as well to handle the physical damage from his basic attacks. If his healing keeps you from finishing him, reduce his healing with Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Warwick.fight: When Warwick E Primal Howl activates, back away, then close the gap again with Hecarim E Devastating Charge after the fear goes off. Start the fight when you have movement speed and Hecarim P Warpath's bonus attack damage.
Warwick.laning: Use your empowered attack to push Warwick toward your team, but build up running distance after activating Hecarim E Devastating Charge before attacking. If an ally's health is below half, Warwick W Blood Hunt reveals their position, so prioritize recalling over forcing a fight.
Warwick.combo: Just before engaging, hit a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage to build stacks. After Warwick E Primal Howl's fear goes off, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run in, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him. After landing, push him back with the empowered attack from the still-active Hecarim E Devastating Charge, then hit him with Hecarim Q Rampage.
Warwick.escape: Don't engage just because Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast is down. Close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows when Warwick R Infinite Duress is still on cooldown and Warwick E Primal Howl's fear has gone off.
Warwick.phase: In the late game, start fights from the flank instead of engaging from the front.
Warwick.teamfight: Keep Warwick R Infinite Duress's long range in mind, and don't leave the side opposite the pit open during an objective standoff. From the flank or behind, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to split the enemy damage dealers. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and heal in the middle of the fight where your team and the enemy are tangled together.

XinZhao.build: Build armor first to withstand Xin Zhao’s main damage. If Xin Zhao P Determination’s healing keeps you from finishing him off, fit Executioner’s Calling into your build after completing one core item.
XinZhao.laning: Use an empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge to knock Xin Zhao toward your allies, but build up distance before hitting him instead of attacking as soon as you activate it. Dodge the thrust from Xin Zhao W Wind Becomes Lightning by moving sideways.
XinZhao.combo: Before engaging, build stacks by hitting a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run in, then charge in with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him, followed by your remaining empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim Q Rampage. Activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread as you reach him to heal during the fight.
XinZhao.escape: Right after Xin Zhao uses Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge is your window to engage with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
XinZhao.phase: Hecarim is strongest in the mid game, when he has attack damage and ability haste. In the late game, avoid engaging from the front and start fights from the side. Counterattack the moment Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard ends.
XinZhao.teamfight: Don’t stand too close to your allies, so Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard’s knockback doesn’t split your formation. From the side or behind, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear the enemy backline. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal where your allies and enemies are clumped together. While Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard is active, don’t unload attacks from outside his spear’s range; use the moment it ends as your chance to counterattack.
XinZhao.fight: Immediately after making Xin Zhao use E Audacious Charge, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Start the fight while Hecarim E Devastating Charge is granting movement speed, and create distance before Xin Zhao Q Three Talon Strike’s third attack. If Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard is active, attack again after its immunity ends.

Zac.watch: Zac E Elastic Slingshot charges before launching him forward to knock you up, so interrupt it with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows when you see him charging. Watch out for the slow and knockup from Zac Q Stretching Strikes, and create distance so you don’t take Zac W Unstable Matter’s max-health damage for long.
Zac.build: Build magic resistance rather than armor to withstand Zac’s main damage. If his healing keeps you from finishing him off, fit Executioner’s Calling into your build after completing one core item. Hecarim P Warpath converts bonus movement speed into attack damage, so fight while you have bonus movement speed.
Zac.laning: Use an empowered attack after building up distance to knock Zac toward your allies. If Zac E Elastic Slingshot is down, use that opening to close the gap.
Zac.combo: If Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows is available, activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run in, then charge with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him, followed by your remaining empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim Q Rampage.
Zac.phase: Hecarim peaks in the mid game, when he has attack damage and ability haste, so look for fights then. In the late game, avoid engaging from the front and start fights from the side.
Zac.escape: The window to go in with Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows is immediately after making Zac use E Elastic Slingshot. You can also interrupt the visible charge with Hecarim E Devastating Charge’s knockback or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows’ fear as you engage.
Zac.fight: Interrupt Zac E Elastic Slingshot’s charge, or engage right after Zac uses it. If you can build up Hecarim Q Rampage stacks beforehand, do so. Once you’re on top of him, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to deal damage and heal. Walk over the blobs Zac leaves behind to prevent his healing and the cooldown reduction for Zac W Unstable Matter.
Zac.teamfight: After withstanding Zac E Elastic Slingshot’s engage, create distance to reduce the damage from Zac W Unstable Matter, which hits nearby targets. Hecarim helps allies engage by using Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows from the flank or behind to fear the enemy damage dealers. After going in, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread amid the clustered allies and enemies to heal, and stomp the blobs Zac leaves behind to destroy them.

Belveth.watch: Bel’Veth W Above and Below knocks you up and slows you, and also resets the cooldown on Bel’Veth Q Void Surge, so sidestep when she closes in. Bel’Veth takes greatly reduced damage while Bel’Veth E Royal Maelstrom is spinning, so focus your damage after it ends.
Belveth.build: Bel’Veth Q Void Surge and Bel’Veth E Royal Maelstrom deal primarily physical damage, so build armor first. If the enemy’s healing keeps you from finishing them off even when you dive, fit Executioner’s Calling into your build after completing one core item.
Belveth.fight: Look for fights early, before Bel’Veth has built up stacks. Engage while Hecarim E Devastating Charge grants you movement speed, and build stacks of Hecarim Q Rampage on a jungle monster just before going in. If Bel’Veth E Royal Maelstrom is active, wait before focusing your damage.
Belveth.laning: Position yourself so an empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge can knock Bel’Veth toward your allies. In early jungle encounters, steal large monsters and camps to slow Bel’Veth’s growth before she can build up growth stacks.
Belveth.escape: Sidestep Bel’Veth W Above and Below, then look for a chance to engage. Before Bel’Veth Q Void Surge comes back up, close the gap with Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear her. If you go in as soon as she uses just one Bel’Veth Q Void Surge, she can escape in another direction.
Belveth.teamfight: From the side or behind, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear the enemy backline and disrupt their formation. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread to heal where your allies and enemies are clumped together. If an ally dies and drops a Void Coral, retreat before Bel’Veth can collect it. Delay the team fight while Bel’Veth is transformed by Bel’Veth R Endless Banquet.
Belveth.combo: Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge and run some distance, then engage with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear the enemy. Follow up with the empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge while it’s still active to knock the enemy back, then use Hecarim Q Rampage. Don’t focus damage while Bel’Veth E Royal Maelstrom is spinning; wait for it to end.
Belveth.phase: Bel’Veth is at her weakest early, so invade and skirmish to steal her camps and slow her growth. Bel’Veth gets stronger over time through permanent growth stacks, so later in the game, don’t insist on taking fights from the same angle; engage from the flank.

Nocturne.watch: When Nocturne R Paranoia activates, don’t get caught alone; immediately move toward your allies. Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror only fears you if its tether stays connected, so create distance with Hecarim E Devastating Charge as soon as it connects. Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness blocks one ability and doubles his attack speed if it does, so check for the shield before using a key ability.
Nocturne.build: Build armor first to withstand Nocturne’s main damage from Nocturne P Umbra Blades, Nocturne Q Duskbringer, and Nocturne R Paranoia. Armor won’t block the magic damage from Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror. If Nocturne’s healing keeps you from finishing him off after a dive, fit Executioner’s Calling into your build after completing one core item.
Nocturne.fight: Start a fight while Hecarim E Devastating Charge grants you movement speed to make use of the attack damage bonus from Hecarim P Warpath. If Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is available, remove the shield first with Hecarim Q Rampage, then use an empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge or Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Nocturne.laning: If Nocturne Q Duskbringer hits you, don’t retreat in a straight line; angle toward an ally or turret until the trail disappears. Keep the river and jungle entrances warded so you know where to retreat before Nocturne R Paranoia activates.
Nocturne.combo: Just before a fight, build stacks by hitting a jungle monster with Hecarim Q Rampage. Activate Hecarim E Devastating Charge out of vision and run in, then use Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and Hecarim Q Rampage as you approach. After confirming that Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness’s shield has been removed, use Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear him, then follow up after landing with your remaining empowered attack from Hecarim E Devastating Charge and Hecarim Q Rampage.
Nocturne.escape: If Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror is down, you can engage without worrying about its tether fear. When Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is down, look for a chance to fear him with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.
Nocturne.phase: Hecarim peaks in the mid game, when he has attack damage and ability haste. In the late game, choose a side engage over a frontal one.
Nocturne.teamfight: When Nocturne R Paranoia darkens your screen, group up with your allies so no one gets isolated. From the side or behind, Hecarim uses Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows to fear the backline and disrupt the enemy formation. After engaging, activate Hecarim W Spirit of Dread in the middle of the fight where your allies are dealing damage to heal.
